# Fixture provenance

`minimal.gxw` is generated from our own byte strings by
`crates/gxw-core/examples/make_fixture.rs` and its `tests/support/mod.rs` helper.
It contains two CFB containers, metadata with a Japanese logical name, a nested
storage, an empty outer stream and an opaque payload. It is **not** a GX Works2
export and contains no valid PLC instructions or vendor data.

To generate a new fixture at a new path:

```sh
cargo run -p gxw-core --example make_fixture -- /tmp/new-minimal.gxw
```

The generator refuses to overwrite an existing file. CFB timestamps may vary;
tests compare the known payloads and structure, not newly generated whole-file hashes.

`raw.gxw` is another generated fixture with the observed simple POU header layout
and three synthetic raw records (`03 ee 03`, `04 9c 01 04`, `03 34 03`). It has no
vendor-authored program or independently validated instruction semantics.

```sh
cargo run -p gxw-core --example make_fixture -- /tmp/new-raw.gxw --raw
```

`third_party/ladder_converter/FX2N.gxw` and `MAIN.csv` are unmodified files from
[ito-soft-design/ladder_converter](https://github.com/ito-soft-design/ladder_converter/tree/f3b26efdfdbf3554a62ef35d86544ccc5628552e/test/files/src).
The publisher describes export using GX Works2 and distributes the paired
project for converter testing. The original MIT license is in `LICENSE.txt`;
revision, source paths and SHA-256 hashes are in `provenance.json`.
`alignment.json` is our derived instruction-to-POU byte alignment using the CSV
operand counts and observed modifier records. It is calibration data, not an
independently generated GX Works2 export or holdout. Tests also parse the
unmodified CSV with Python's standard library to check row/operand interpretation.

The pair contains 170 instructions (416 raw records). Of these, 83 cover all
15 supported basic opcodes. Other observed records identify boundaries only;
the whole project is not treated as supported. No third-party source code was
copied into the parser. These fixtures and their license travel together in
the sdist; wheels contain neither the fixtures nor the alignment files.

`ladder/*.csv` are four small test inputs transcribed from circuit diagrams in
Mitsubishi's FX programming manual JY997D16601R, printed pages 200–203
(ORB, ANB, MPS/MRD/MPP and cascaded outputs). The matching JSON files record
manually derived contact paths, polarities and output instructions, together
with the source URL and page. They use synthetic step numbers and add END when
the printed excerpt omits it. They are **not native GX Works2 CSV exports**, and
they do not validate native binary decoding. No manual text, PDF or circuit
image is distributed. Circuit topology checks and native GXW/CSV alignment are
separate validation layers.

`simulation/*.csv` are six hand-authored/transcribed bit programs.
`simulation/scenarios.json` contains 29 expected scan states, the mnemonic source,
and provenance. The double-coil and SET/RST inputs follow printed pp. 170 and 215
of JY997D16601R; self-holding, reversed SET/RST, saved-read and cascade variants
include independent Boolean/state recurrences. END and step numbers are synthetic.
The previous `ladder/*.json` printed path oracles additionally serve as Boolean
execution oracles over all X-input combinations. These inputs are not native
CSV exports, unseen GXW holdouts, or captured GX Simulator2/hardware traces.

`timing/*.csv` contains seven authored timer/counter inputs, shared by eight
scenarios in `timing/scenarios.json`. Their 71 fixed operations cover clock
boundaries, K0, retention, reset, counter saturation and period changes. Device
ranges and basic behavior use JY997D16601R printed pp. 38, 41, 86, 98–100,
103–104 and 215. Expected values are explicitly authored for the scheduling and
reset rules in `docs/timing.md`; no expected values are captured from the core.
These CSVs do not establish native T/C binary encodings or hardware equivalence.
# Structured control

`structured.gxw` is self-authored, generated by
`cargo run -p gxw-core --example structured_fixture --locked`.
It contains two blocks, NO/NC contacts, a coil, an opaque FB instance, ports,
wires and a local declaration with Japanese/HTML-sensitive text. It is a binary
layout control, not a GX Works2-produced project or PLC execution oracle. The
Rust test verifies regeneration byte-for-byte. Upstream manufacturer templates
and independently downloaded projects are kept outside the public fixtures.
